summary:
Why Luna is slow. In the 19.3 h Luna run (skill-craft 1.16.1), planning took 647 of 1,158 minutes, and Luna was generating tokens 99.5% of the time. Waiting was about 2%. Sonnet plans the same request from the same prompts in about 5 minutes. So prompt length is not the cause, and cutting prompt text will not speed Luna up. I recommend deleting none of it. The cost is how much Luna writes and re-reads at effort max. Your 2026-09-27 rule already says E2E runs use xhigh, yet both Luna battleship runs used max. Fixing that needs no code, only the flag.

What changes. Backchain defaults to one pass. One option, --backchain-passes one|converge|none, is recorded in state.md like --lint. 'one' is the default. 'converge' restores today's behaviour. 'none' offers no whole loop at plan. One pass saves about 92 to 94 minutes (8%) of a run like that one. 'none' saves about 128 (11%). About 17 hours would remain, still past the 10 h session limit. Improve review loops (about 190 minutes) stay as they are, because their later passes found real defects.

What it may cost. Backchain passes 2 to 5 each reported a finding: a confirmation level, two confirmation clauses, a metadata label. A single pass leaves defects of that kind. The script check will not catch them, since it passes the plan graph before and after every pass. Also, no later stage reads the plan graph, and Improve's review does not open it. So even one pass buys unproven value. 'none' is the cut the evidence favours, and 'one' is what you asked for.

Do first: (1) decide effort. (2) Record a dated S-10 carve-out in its own commit. (3) Replay one pass on the saved 1.16.1 inputs at max and xhigh before any 10-hour run, to see what one pass finds and whether Luna reports done. (4) Then build and release as one batch.
diagnosis:
RUN [M]: Luna gpt-6-luna at effort max (invocation.json), battleship, skill-craft 1.16.1, 1,158.5 min (19.3 h): timeline.json starts 2026-10-03T22:54:02Z, last accept 2026-10-04T18:12:34Z. Planning window (intake to the first test-spec accept) 647.5 min = 55.9%. The v1200 run also used max (its invocation.json), and the owner's note luna-is-gpt-6 (2026-09-27) says ShipLoop E2E runs use xhigh because at max planning was too slow and 'the cost was per-pass effort, not loop count'.

PASSES vs PER-CALL THINKING vs WAITING [M, scratchpad reports 0 to 2, 2 rollouts, 2,919 responses]. Waiting is about 2% (tool execution 3.0 min, gaps between sessions 3.1 min, one 12-min stall). Luna generating is 1,152 min (99.5%): 89% output decode at about 55 tokens/s, 7.6% fixed per call, 3.3% input context. Per-call thinking is large: 2,276 small or message-only responses are 52.3% of output tokens (1.245M reasoning tokens, about 376 min, 32.5% of wall clock). Passes and thinking overlap, not add: a pass is a set of calls, and thinking is the length of each call. Repeat passes in the planning window cost about 249 min (38%): Backchain passes 2..N 152.6 min plus Improve passes 2..n at the planning children 118.6 min (rounded).

LOOPS [M]. Five loop stages (spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan, test-spec) = 592.3 of 647.5 min: Backchain 263.5 (44.5%: plan loop passes 11/15/26/18/17/12/4 min = 103 by the ledger and 106 by file mtimes, step-plan passes 42/55/6/4, plus about 50 min prep and result writing across both), Improve loops 188.8 (31.9%), Improve opening files 29.7 (5.0%), producer work 110.5 (18.7%). Ledger and mtime sources differ by up to 7 min per pass; loop totals agree within 3%.

NOT PACKETS [M]: Sonnet 5.5 planned the same request in 4.8 min and 83 turns with same-shaped packets (1.16.0). It wrote a 0.8 KB plan against Luna's 32.1 KB, ran no Backchain loop, and ran 24 Improve passes in 5.6 min against Luna's 41 in 305 to 360. Per Improve pass that is 0.23 min against 8.8 (about 38 times) with 1.7 times the passes. At 1.20.0 the plan packet's Backchain text is 480 words and the audit-stage text 301 [M, counted]. Input context is 3.3% of latency, so byte trims cannot deliver the speed-up.

WHAT THE BACKCHAIN PASSES DID, RE-CHECKED THIS REVISION [M]. The done packets show passes 1 to 5 classified non-trivial and exit unsatisfied, pass 6 trivial and unsatisfied, pass 7 trivial and satisfied (complete). Pass 1 edited 14 of 20 steps (F-1 wrong supplier direction, F-2 API-concurrency obligation, F-3 browser recovery report criteria, and browser fixture/UI confirmation levels corrected to execute). Pass 2 F-4 changed S2's confirmation level inspect to execute (0 bytes), the same class pass 1 had just fixed elsewhere. Pass 3 F-5 changed S4's confirm clause (+198 B) and found a T42 gap in the lens index. Pass 4 F-6 changed S11's ambiguous no-npm confirmation (+224 B). Pass 5 F-7 corrected a source-provenance label in scratch metadata. Passes 6 and 7 changed nothing. No edge, goal, supplier or produce changed after pass 1.

THE SCRIPT CHECK DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE AT PLAN [M, I ran shiploop_backchain_graph.check]. It returns ok with no failures and 0 unconfirmed produces on all four plan-loop candidates: generator-draft.json (f33a46ef), the true pre-loop candidate 9e321e3d (recovered from pass-01-audit-input.md; its digest equals the freeze log's), pass 1's output b66d62f0 (elaborated-candidate.json), and the final 3853b978. It passes before pass 1 and after every pass, and it models none of F-1..F-7. Only the step-plan candidates fail it, on invariant 4 (orphan discovered step D1). Even the final step-plan candidate still fails, so four model passes and Improve accepted D1. That loop is no longer offered whole at 1.20.0 (BACKCHAIN_NATIVE_CALLS has only plan), and the check is record-only (nothing refuses a failing check). Both attacks called elaborated-candidate.json the pre-loop candidate; it is pass 1's output, but their conclusion holds on the true pre-loop file.

THE PLAN-STAGE GRAPH IS AN ISLAND [M]. No later packet names scratch/backchain-plan (0 of the run's packets; 7 packets name scratch/backchain-step-plan). Pass logs say the passes changed only scratch artifacts ('Candidate graph and prose plan were not edited'; plan.md stayed untracked until Improve's commit 6be28af). The plan-stage Improve child's bind file has 0 mentions of Backchain, and its receipt lists the scratch files only as evidence refs after the fact. So Improve reviews plan.md, not the graph, and the repairs in the graph never reached any consumer. The host also hand-rolled its graph checks in every pass (every pass log says 'structural status unknown'; a local Kahn check had a bug in pass 6). With backchain-check printed since 1.19.0, part of the 12 to 26 min per pass may fall, unmeasured [I].

CONTRACT SIZE [M]: the host-written plan contract was 7,716 B and the step-plan contract 11,924 B against the 9,216 B budget.

CAVEATS: n=1 per cell; stage times vary about 2x run to run. The v1200 run is not live: events.jsonl last written 17:14:32 PDT, it is 18:02 now, and the owner's memory says it was killed at about 48 min and must never be resumed. It gives no loop evidence, so 1.20.0's trim (3592b195) is unmeasured on Luna.
backchain_single_pass:
KNOB [M]: a printed text in two or three variants, selected by one run option. No ShipLoop script writes, reads or checks the Backchain child's Until Loop contract (check_terminal is wired only to the test and quality loops, _ephemeral_terminal_packet only to Improve; backchain-check never gates). The pass count is set by two things the host copies: required_trivial_reviews from the ShipLoop packet and the exit wording from skills/backchain/references/convergence.md ('Frozen plan-only child contract'). The 1.16.1 host-written exit ('after two distinct complete trivial/no-change reviews since the latest reset') mirrors convergence.md, not the packet. Changing only the number would fail: under that exit text Luna reported unsatisfied through pass 6. So the packet text, convergence.md, caller-contract.md and Backchain SKILL.md change in ONE commit (increment I2) so the tree never tells the host gate 0 in one place and gate 2 in another.

FLAG AND HOME: run option backchain_passes in state.md, values one (default), converge, none. CLI --backchain-passes on init and workspace start (passthrough exists for lint). A recovery retry cannot change it (copy of _require_retry_lint). No mid-run --set (KISS: the contract is written per loop; a new run is the route). A saved run without the key is refused by the generic missing-fields refusal in _validate_current_state once the key is in _STATE_KEYS, with FRESH_RUN_HINT (no separate _need). Plumbing mirrors lint: _STATE_KEYS, new_state, validation, shiploop_protocol argparse, and shiploop_prompts.prompt(stage, delegation, backchain_passes) and _backchain_guidance(stage, backchain_passes) with default one, so the module-level BACKCHAIN_GUIDANCE and PROMPTS render the default. shiploop_navigator_dry_run takes the mode too.

TEXT, mode one, plan stage (replaces the 23-word gate clause; 94 words counted, net about +70): 'Backchain passes: one. Write the child's start contract with `required_trivial_reviews: 0` and this exit condition verbatim, appending only case-specific clauses: One complete dependency review/fix/check cycle has run; every finding of that cycle is repaired within the edit bounds; every `Confirm by` clause meets the planning guide's Outcomes rule; the printed `backchain-check` is ok on the final candidate and its receipt is cited; final candidate-specific domain evidence is saved. A pass that completes that cycle reports `exit_assessment: satisfied` even when it repaired the candidate; Until Loop then completes the child and no second review runs.' The printed JSON field is the literal contract field. The packet also tells the host to put the line `Backchain passes: one` beside the existing binding marker in the child's `work` (about 10 words). The dropped draft sentence 'report unsatisfied only for a named open gap' steered the one field the gate-0 runtime trusts; the exit text now defines when it holds. The Outcomes clause ties pass 1 to the confirmation-level and two-people-test duties that F-4 to F-6 showed pass 1 can miss.

Audit stages (spec, step-plan, carry-forward, product-acceptance), mode one: one 16-word pointer in the repair/revise sentence, 'A repair/revise child runs one review/fix/check cycle (`Backchain passes: one`, as Backchain's convergence reference defines it)', with no literal gate field, so the pin test_audit_stages_offer_the_audit_and_one_bounded_repair_and_not_the_loop_text (audit text must not name required_trivial_reviews) stays true. Mode converge prints today's text unchanged.

MODE none (increment I3): at plan the packet prints the audit route instead of the loop text, and the navigator prints only the audit resource plus the loop-resource status line (the resource block's condition becomes stage in BACKCHAIN_NATIVE_CALLS and mode is not none). The sentence 'A whole plan/draft is requested only at plan' becomes 'No whole plan/draft is requested in this run (`Backchain passes: none`)'. Counted: plan guidance 480 words becomes about 301 (-179, not the 480 one attack claimed), and the six-file Backchain/Until Loop read at plan (12 reads, 109 KB in 1.16.1) is not requested. A read-only audit is still available, and a repair/revise after a finding runs one pass.

SELECTION CHANNEL FOR STANDALONE BACKCHAIN: the backchain-caller/v1 packet is a closed shape with no gate field, so no field is added. The caller states the choice in the child request as the marker line `Backchain passes: one`, next to the existing 'Backchain standalone Until Loop binding:' marker. convergence.md, caller-contract.md and Backchain SKILL.md (description, 'Source-aware native plan' step 4, Procedure step 4) become: default two consecutive trivial reviews and both qualifying records; with the marker, one cycle, gate 0, one review record plus the backchain-check receipt as the terminal evidence set. caller-contract.md's 'a terminal receipt with only the latest review recoverable is incomplete planning' applies to the default only. harness.md needs no edit (its only hit is 'second review controller'). Standalone callers keep default two. ShipLoop SKILL.md and backchain-planning.md replace their literal 'required_trivial_reviews: 2 ... two consecutive' with a pointer to the packet's printed gate, so the gate is defined once in the packet and once in convergence.md (S-12).

WHAT ONE PASS MEANS [M, my own re-run of the vendored runtime plus two independent ones]: gate 0 plus an exit the host can assess as satisfied after one cycle. The first review reviews, repairs inside the same pass, runs the checks on the repaired candidate, reports non-trivial with exit satisfied, and the runtime completes (verified: gate 0, non-trivial and satisfied completes after 1 action). If the first pass changes the candidate, nothing independently re-reviews that repair: its evidence is the cycle's own review record, the backchain-check receipt on the repaired candidate (structural only, see diagnosis) and the later Improve child, which reviews plan.md and not the graph. Gate 0 is a first-class runtime mode: its next-action text branches on gate 0, and skills/shiploop/references/execution-planning.md already uses required_trivial_reviews 0 for per-step Until Loop children [M]. At gate 2 the runtime already completes a trivial first pass that left the tree unchanged, so today's best case with a changing first pass is 3 passes, and 1.16.1 took 7.

NOT A HARD CAP [M]: unsatisfied or unknown continues, blocked stops, unresolved plus satisfied is refused, and the runtime has no max-iterations or budget field (a contract carrying one is refused as an invalid schema). A conservative host that reports unsatisfied after the changing pass completes at its next satisfied report, so about 2 passes, not 7 [I: the runtime side is verified, the host's behaviour is not]. Gate 1 is not one pass (a repair is non-trivial and still needs a clean pass after it); it saves only about 9 min on the 1.16.1 run.

PER-OUTCOME CONFIRMATIONS: still an authoring obligation in pass 1 (backchain-planning.md Outcomes: confirmation per criterion, two-people test, exercised or inspected, command-checkable content criteria). The exit now names that rule, so the level and wording defects that passes 2 to 4 later fixed become pass 1's duty. What is dropped is later passes re-hardening them after the fact.

VENDORED RUNTIME [M]: untouched. test/improve.test.sh pins the sha256 of ADAPTER.md, until_loop_ephemeral.py and runtime-ephemeral.md in PROVENANCE.json, and contract values are not vendored. required_trivial_reviews is the runtime's own field, so Backchain's rule of never supplying a pass ceiling or counter is not violated.

NOT ENFORCED: no script checks that the host wrote gate 0, and a host that writes 2 anyway is not caught at write time. Mitigations: the pre-release replay (R0) shows what Luna writes; the Run Review export already shows 'Trivial streak x of y required' from the runtime receipt, and I4 adds the option and the check-receipt digest fact (record-only). A script-written contract (a02) waits for evidence and must accept a gate-0 complete packet whose last report is non-trivial; check_loop_packet and _ephemeral_terminal_packet cannot be reused unchanged.

spec_and_owner_rules:
TENSIONS [M unless marked]. (1) SPEC S-10 says quality, test and review loops run until a stated, checkable condition with a frozen contract the script writes and iterations the script counts, with no iteration cap. A one-pass default for the Backchain planning child is a different stated exit, not a numeric cap, but it relaxes S-10 and S-9 for that loop, so SPEC 'Change admission' requires the spec amended first, in its own commit (I0). S-9 says completion is never 'the model's own judgment'; at gate 0 completion is one model report. That is also true today of the 'trivial' classification that drives gate 2, and the check is structural and record-only, so the carve-out says plainly that S-9 holds for this loop only in that structural sense. S-4, S-5 and S-12 (hand-built loop contracts count as model_glue in metrics.py GLUE_CONTRACT) are already unmet for Backchain (a02); the carve-out names that as a standing, accepted exception. (2) Owner memory 'ShipLoop loops unbounded' (no cap, no revise/blocked for running long) is written for quality and test loops; narrow it to them, and ask the owner to edit the note (this task edits no memory). (3) 'Steps iterate until a stated check confirms each exit criterion' and the LLM 80% postulate (one pass leaves 0.2, two 0.04): partly conflicts. For this loop the data say the structural gap closed in pass 1 and passes 2 to 5 reported confirmation-level or wording findings, so the postulate binds here more than the earlier draft said; Improve's data (three warranted fixes in passes 1 to 3 at test-strategy) supports it, which is why Improve stays. The owner's override is explicit for Backchain only. (4) 'Test pass is the evidence': the one-pass exit is model-assessed. backchain-check is record-only and passes the plan graph before pass 1, so at plan it does not discriminate. This conflict is larger than the earlier draft said; it is flagged, not built (a02). (5) 'Enterprise rigour is standard': a confirming review of a planning aid is not tests, security or ownership; those stay. (6) 'Verbose prompts over size bounds' and 'prompts concise, meaningful change' against 'cut them down': no justified guidance is deleted; mode one adds about 70 words at plan and 16 at each audit stage, mode none removes 179 at plan [M counted]. (7) KISS: option plus text; no --set, no script contract, Improve untouched, no missing-key special case. (8) One supported version: the new state key refuses older saved runs with FRESH_RUN_HINT; no migration. (9) Adversarial-review-loop and SPEC admission: each change records evaluation, anchor, non-regression, evidence; verbose commit and journal entry citing related commits 3592b195, e0aeaa2d, 112b239c, db61a4a7, 931c53e2, 6a997a02. (10) Batch-run-to-completion and the E2E session's hold: one batch, one release, one verification run; no push, release.py or run launch until that session says its planning-speed release is out. (11) test-the-route-not-the-wording: the one-pass exit is exercised through the real vendored runtime (I2) and through a real host (R0).

SUPERSEDES in docs/shiploop-backchain-validator-comparison-plan-2026-10-04.md (mark in I0, with date and reason): section 1's 'The exit rule (two clean passes, no pass cap) is S-10 and stays unless the spec is amended first', the same words in iteration I6, expectation B1 'every pass earns its time', and the policy-table lines 'no pass cap'. The loop policy for plan is now owner-decided for Backchain; the Track 1/2 comparison still measures what a loop adds.

ADVERSARIAL EVALUATION, one line each (consequence: disposition). Weakens S-9/S-10: accepted by carve-out, no cap added. Lost material finding: accepted for Backchain by owner decision (passes 2 to 5 non-trivial but confirmation-level or wording only; none reached a consumer); Improve unchanged. quality_risk:
WHAT LATER PASSES CAUGHT [M, re-checked this revision]. Plan loop passes 2 to 5 were each classified non-trivial: F-4 a confirmation level (inspect to execute, 0 bytes; pass 1's F-3 had just fixed the same class on other steps, so pass 1 did not converge on it), F-5 an S4 confirm clause (+198 B) plus a T42 lens-index gap, F-6 an S11 ambiguous confirmation (+224 B), F-7 a source-provenance label. Passes 6 and 7 changed nothing. The earlier draft measured this in bytes (422 B), which hides a verification-level fix and a screen gap; classification is the right measure. No edge, goal, supplier or produce changed after pass 1.

THE ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: an unreviewed set of confirmation-level and wording defects of the F-4, F-5, F-6 kind, in a graph that no later stage consumes and Improve does not open [M]. Mitigation: the one-pass exit names the Outcomes rule (two-people test, exercised or inspected), so pass 1 is told to do what F-4 to F-6 showed it can miss. This is a mitigation, not a net. Improve at plan reviews plan.md (replayability, weaker stand-ins, missing prerequisite) and had already fixed the AC-01 no-npm class in the test strategy about 2 h before F-5 and F-6, but that is plausible cover only. Whether any clean confirming pass ever prevented a defect is unknown (no counterfactual).

THE SCRIPT CHECK IS NOT A COMPENSATOR AT PLAN [M]. It passes the plan graph before pass 1 (9e321e3d), after pass 1 and at the end, and models none of F-1..F-7. D1-class defects (orphan discovered step) belong to the step-plan loop: all four of its candidates fail invariant 4, including the final one, and 1.20.0 offers no whole step-plan loop. For them the check is the only net, and it is record-only. Step-plan pass 2's F-03 and F-04 (packet-required items) matter only if that loop recurs.

NOT COVERED BY ANYTHING ELSE: a pass-1 repair the check does not model (a semantic dependency error, an omitted outcome) has no second review. The residual is accepted by the owner for Backchain.

FAILURE MODES THAT KEEP THE COST: the host writes required_trivial_reviews 2 (silent); the host reports unsatisfied after a changing pass (about 2 passes [I]); Luna starts an unrequested loop at step-plan.

HOW A LOSS WOULD SHOW (same case, host, model, effort): (1) R0 before release: findings of one pass against F-1..F-7, the reported exit_assessment, the gate written, minutes, at max and xhigh. (2) Next run, Backchain loop doc: passes 1, gate 0, final complete; the option beside the written gate. (3) Check receipts on the first and last candidate snapshots: whether the check ever discriminates at plan, and whether the last receipt's candidate_sha256 equals the loop's final candidate digest. (4) Downstream finding classes and counts at the plan, step-plan and test-spec Improve children against 1.16.1 (plan 3 passes: marginal, clean, clean; step-plan #1: marginal, clean, clean); more dependency, supplier or orphan findings means the loss moved downstream. (5) Downstream refusals and replays: revisions, planning_reconciliations, revise outcomes, system-test failures traced to a plan defect. (6) Rubric-eval judgement of plan and step-plan artifacts against 1.16.1 under criteria pre-registered in I0; per the eval rule a material quality difference trumps speed, near-identical quality prefers fewer tokens then less time, standard scales, no invented thresholds. Sonnet runs no Backchain loop, so it cannot show a Backchain quality loss.
